answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by binding each identity to exclusive control of a unique optical prism housed on a remote private island haven, where live spectral measurements must be attested continuously. Peers verify the prism's non-shareable hardware signature and the latency of island-specific environmental data that cannot be pooled or multiplexed across clones. An attacker fails because acquiring separate exclusive prisms for each fake identity imposes a linear hardware cost that scales without amortization, enforced on-chain by rejecting mismatched live proofs.
